cross_project.why: kevinsawicki and tootallnate together have zero not-flaky documents (see decisions/09-index-contents.md), so querying either as the held-out project produces a 100%-flaky query population where precision@k trivially equals the majority baseline (both 1.0) -- not evidence of discrimination. The one direction that would be informative, holding out square-okhttp (the only project with real class balance) and indexing the other two, cannot run at all: those two projects contribute no not-flaky documents to build a two-class training index from.

kevinsawicki-http-request.note: uninformative: query population is 100% flaky (kevinsawicki has zero not-flaky documents), so this number cannot distinguish real discrimination from guessing the majority class

tootallnate-java-websocket.note: uninformative, for the same reason as kevinsawicki-http-request above
